chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather Al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Repay the entrustments, even if it be to a murderer of the children of the Prophets.'
ai.seo_question: What does Islam say about returning trusts to enemies?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith chains back to Imam al-Sadiq, who attributes the ruling to Imam Ali, establishing a strong prophetic lineage for this principle of universal fidelity. It underscores the Shia scholarly view that the obligation of amanah is independent of the recipient's merit or enmity, ensuring that justice is not compromised by personal grievance even against those hostile to the Ahl al-Bayt.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Al Qasim Bin yahya, from his grandfather Al Hassan Bin Rashid, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>
having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Repay the entrustments even though it be to a murderer of the children of the Prophets<sup>as</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Khalid from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya from his grandfather, al-Hassan ibn Rashid from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
Amir al-Mu’minin, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘You must return a trust even if an assassin of the children of the prophet has left it with you.’”
